topic: WCTX: Cross-Repository Context for Coding Agents via Local MCP

key_points: Local-first MCP server that turns completed coding-agent sessions into structured, evidence-backed engineering context
Solves the core problem: a session in repo A discovers a bug in repo B, but a fresh session in repo B a week later has lost that knowledge
7 MCP tools ordered for progressive disclosure: workspace_overview, search_session_evidence, get_evidence, get_session_evidence, get_related_repositories, verify_finding_freshness, finalize_session
Core concepts: Workspace (logical product above repos), Repository, Relation (directional typed edges like uses/depends_on/calls/imports), Session, Evidence, Freshness (git-based staleness verdict)
Local-first: no cloud account, no embeddings, no transcript upload; SQLite + FTS5 + git
Session adapters for Xirp, Claude Code, Codex, and generic JSONL
wctx capture --summary / wctx search commands; wctx instructions --write installs guidance into CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md
Requires Node 22+ and git; MIT license; TypeScript
Persistent memory for AI coding agents; single Go binary, SQLite + FTS5, zero dependencies
Exposed through CLI, HTTP API, MCP, and interactive TUI; works with Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Codex, VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf
Agent-agnostic local memory; strong single-project focus, does not emphasize multi-repository topology or transcript-derived provenance
~5,991 stars (checked 2026-08-13)
Broad automatic capture: 12 lifecycle hooks, 54 MCP tools, embeddings + hybrid retrieval, session replay
Global memory server shared across agents (localhost:3111)
Documents a real trap: Claude Code's cleanupPeriodDays (default 30) deletes JSONL transcripts, so import-only capture silently loses old history
Nearest neighbour: multi-repo workspaces with workspace.yaml, persistent observations + decisions (ADRs with supersession lifecycle), FTS, freshness
Auto-capture hooks: git post-commit and Claude Code PostToolUse; workspace detect-links infers cross-repo edges from Python imports and OpenAPI/protobuf/GraphQL contracts
Unit of memory is an observation written at commit/edit time; edges inferred from code/contracts rather than declared
Repo and org memory from GitHub PR history, with confidence, freshness, and cross-repo impact
strict:true + minConfidence returns 'No reliable historical evidence found' rather than weak matches (fail-closed posture)
PRs record what was merged; does not index the investigation (dead ends, unresolved questions); needs GitHub auth
Nightly 'dreaming' daemon that consolidates finished Claude Code transcripts into durable facts
Review-gated updates and pre-registered evaluation bars; closest in philosophy (post-session processing beats in-session discipline)
Single-agent / single-store in scope

stats.fact: On a synthetic 15-query, 28-evidence-item corpus, the relevant prior session appeared in the top five for 15 of 15 queries and ranked first for 11 of 15.

Adding workspace topology to plain FTS5 improved MRR from 0.839 to 0.867, made repository attribution exact (0.93 to 1.00), and eliminated results from unrelated repositories (0.20 to 0.00 per query).
Median local retrieval latency is 1.57 ms with a median response payload of ~5.0 KB (~1,250 tokens for five results) in the shipped configuration.
Source attribution was complete for 100% of returned results under all three evaluation configurations: every result carried its session id, repository, and commit.
wctx is a local-first MCP server: no cloud account, no embeddings, no transcript upload; uses SQLite + FTS5 + git for storage and freshness checks.
wctx exposes 7 MCP tools ordered for progressive disclosure to stay affordable in a context window, versus agentmemory's 54 tools.
Claude Code's cleanupPeriodDays (default 30) deletes JSONL transcripts, so import-only capture silently loses old history — wctx copies the raw transcript into its own data directory at import time.
wctx requires Node 22+ and git; install via pnpm install && pnpm build, then wctx init and wctx doctor; MCP setup via 'claude mcp add wctx -- wctx mcp'.

angles: The core pain: coding-agent sessions are scoped to a repository, but the system under investigation is not — knowledge discovered in one repo is lost to fresh sessions in related repos.
Post-session processing beats in-session discipline: agents skip save_memory calls under load, so import and audit the transcript instead.
Local-first and privacy: no cloud account, no embeddings, no transcript upload — a differentiator versus cloud/vector-based memory tools.
Freshness as a first-class concept: git-based staleness verdict (current / possibly_stale / stale / unknown) tells agents when evidence is no longer trustworthy.
Declared relations over inferred ones: directional typed edges (uses, depends_on, calls, imports) drive explainable ranking and human-readable reasons.
Progressive disclosure: 7 tools instead of 54 keeps the MCP surface affordable in a context window.
Making it proactive: installing guidance into CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md so agents search before investigating and record root causes, decisions, and unresolved questions.
Security posture: redaction of secrets, evidence labelled as historical untrusted data, argument-array git calls, constructed FTS5 queries.
